title: Webbing and stitching materials survey
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers; optional clip-on Shoulder Module or one-piece Integrated Harness) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards (cite by number and title only), never name private individuals or incident victims, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. Tethers, belts and straps need webbing with known strength, elongation, UV, chlorine and abrasion behaviour (REQ-L2, REQ-D1).
objective: Compare polyester, nylon, Dyneema/UHMWPE and aramid webbing and thread types using public datasheets and literature: strength, elongation at load, UV and water/chlorine degradation, abrasion, cost class, and suppliers that publish specs.
acceptanceCriteria: Properties table with source per value
Discusses stitch patterns (bar-tack, W-box) and their published efficiencies
Every factual claim has a cited, working source link; estimates are labelled as estimates
